title: Where the Waters Divide
subtitle: Flat Clustering · k-means (assignment + choosing k)
story: They called themselves the Assay — an order of alchemists who held that all things, base and worthy alike, could be reduced to their true kinds and sorted, the worthy kept and the rest poured away. To feed their great engine they bled a whole valley of its water, and tore from its people the Wellheart — a living stone the vale-folk say holds the first clean water, that had kept their springs sweet for a thousand years. The springs have run bitter ever since. The Assay are long gone now, and their engine — a drowned waterworks at the bottom of a flooded shaft, that parts distilled essences into sacred pools — is failing, the cistern filling. You have come to take the Wellheart back and carry it home to the vale. But the engine keeps its makers' conceit, and opens only to one who can sort as they did. Climb down its bridges and ladders, throw the diverters that turn the falling water aside, and answer the reading at each of its fonts. Reach the drowned floor before the water does, read the last of the Assay's sorting, and bring the Wellheart back into the light.

done.title: The engine turns over
done.body: The last diverter grinds home under your hands, and deep below a sluice the Assay meant never to be reached gives way. The falling water finds new channels; the way down clears to the drowned floor. The engine is finishing the sort its makers died believing in — and the vault at the bottom, with the Wellheart sealed inside it, is finally within reach.

escapeDone.title: Out, and the Wellheart with you
escapeDone.body: You wade the rising floor and see the Assay's work whole at last: every thread of falling water gathered into its own great pool, the essences parted into their kinds — three in one, two in another, four in the last. You read the sort the way its makers would have, set the reckoning into the vault, and it yields. You lift the Wellheart from its cradle and climb the rising passage as the water closes over the engine behind you — out into daylight, the Assay's cold conceit turned against them at last, and the vale's first clean water on its way home.
escapeDone.note: PROVISIONAL: the counts (3,2,4) and the lock code are placeholders keyed to what the basin ART depicts; fix once the scene is generated. The escape is data-free / independent of the reliquary_phials dataset.

coverPrompt: Minimalist stylised thumbnail poster of a lone circular temple cistern seen from directly above: one dark round shaft opening downward, three small still pools glowing warm amber deep at its base, thin threads of falling water between them, a cool teal stone ring around. One bold high-contrast silhouette, iconic and uncluttered, minimal detail. Flat limited palette: deep teal, icy blue, one warm amber glow. Soft film grain, painterly but clean, strong negative space, single centred focal subject. No people, no text, no lettering, no logos. Square composition.

debrief.title: How this world worked
debrief.intro: The whole engine was one idea the Assay built into stone and water: flat clustering — sorting many things into a few true kinds by which they most belong together. Every font you answered was one move of it, every diverter an assignment, and the flooded floor was the result laid bare — the essences gathered into k groups, waiting only to be read. The Assay used the sort to decide what was worthy of keeping; you used the very same skill to walk out with everything they kept.

rooms.title: The catwalk and the viewing port
rooms.technique: orientation — read the whole structure before acting
rooms.debrief: Before you touched a thing, the viewing port showed you the whole shaft as one picture — every falling stream, every drowned bridge, the pools far below. Standing back to see the whole structure at once, before you act, is where every clustering begins.

authoring.scenePrompt: This is a panorama. A 360-degree view from the centre of a swaying rope-and-plank catwalk strung across the very top of a vast circular stone shaft that plunges down into darkness, the scene wrapping continuously all the way around so the left and right edges meet seamlessly. Ahead, a heavy brass viewing port is bolted into the catwalk rail — a round downward-angled lens faintly aglow with a schematic amber light, as if a map were lit inside it. To one side, a mossy stone post and a heavy coil of ancient rope mark where the catwalk meets the shaft wall. Set into the shaft wall opposite, a carved archway — the closed way down — with coiled rope ladders beside it. Around the rest of the ring, ancient teal-streaked stonework, slack guide ropes, and far overhead a narrow disc of deep dusk sky letting a shaft of cold light down; below the catwalk, waterfall-threads spill from openings in the walls and vanish into the dark. Cold dusk light from above against warm amber lamp-glow, deep teal shadow, drifting spray and mist, painterly, cinematic, richly detailed. No people, no lettering, no captions, no text.
authoring.doorPrompt: The carved archway down now stands open, revealing a first flight of wet stone steps and a rope ladder descending into amber-lit gloom deeper in the shaft; the viewing port's glow and the dusk light from above are unchanged. Same painterly teal-and-amber style, no people, no lettering, no text.

rooms.title: The first reading-landing

entry.title: The first font
entry.text: Down the first ladder, and the water's roar closes overhead. A stone font juts from the landing, a tray of the Assay's phials jammed in its basin, the diverter beside it dead until the font is answered. The engine will not let you pass on trust — only on a reading.

rooms.debrief: This landing was one decision of the sort: which pool a stream of samples belongs to. Solving it and throwing the diverter committed that assignment, and the water below fell differently for it.

authoring.scenePrompt: This is a panorama. A 360-degree view from the centre of a broad stone landing partway down a vast flooded shaft — a junction where three ways meet — the scene wrapping continuously all the way around so the left and right edges meet seamlessly. Ahead, a low carved reading-font of dark stone, its surface a shallow scrying-basin of still water aglow with faint chart-like amber light — the place where the phials are read. To one side, a makers' diverter lever set in a stone housing. Three ways lead off the landing, each a rope bridge or ladder with a thread of waterfall sheeting across it: a rope ladder climbing UP toward the catwalk and its high disc of dusk sky; a ladder dropping DOWN into the gloom toward a lower landing; and a long rope bridge running straight ACROSS the open gulf of the shaft to a far landing at the same height. Around the rest of the ring, teal-streaked pillars, falling water threading down through the shaft, wet ledges and coiled rope. Warm amber font-glow against cool teal shaft-shadow, a thin disc of dusk sky far above, drifting spray, painterly, cinematic, richly detailed. No people, no lettering, no captions, no text.

entry.title: Deeper, a subtler test
entry.text: Lower, dimmer, the sky a coin of dusk far above. This font asks less kindly than the last: not how large a kind is, but how many true kinds there even are. The Assay set it to turn away anyone who could only count what they were handed.

rooms.designNote: PUZZLE (verified). Dataset reliquary_phials. TYPE 4 PICK-THE-POINT (click the elbow) — for puzzle-type variety. The student plots within-cluster spread vs k and CLICKS the elbow. starterCode: reliquary_phials. pick.plotCode (WebR, ggiraph): wss <- sapply(1:6, function(k) kmeans(reliquary_phials[,c('clarity','mineral','resin','ash')], centers=k, nstart=25)$tot.withinss); df <- data.frame(k=1:6, wss=wss); p <- ggplot(df, aes(k, wss)) + geom_line() + ggiraph::geom_point_interactive(aes(data_id=k, tooltip=k), size=4) + labs(x='number of families (k)', y='within-cluster spread'). pick.prompt: 'Adding families always tightens the clusters a little — but only up to a point. Plot the within-cluster spread against k and click the ELBOW: the k past which more families barely help.' ANSWER: the point at k=3 (WSS 37689 -> 11667 -> 966 [elbow] -> 810 -> 661 -> 543; the drop collapses after 3). Solving UNLOCKS diverter S2 -> D2. Mid shaft. NEW ART.

rooms.title: The cast-off gallery

entry.title: The cast-off gallery
entry.text: A bridge out from the second landing ends not at a font but at a reeking side-gallery — the Assay's spillway, where all they judged base was sluiced away. No reading waits here, only their cold accounting of everything they threw out, and a ladder dropping on into the dark.

rooms.technique: flavour — the discard stream (no graded puzzle)
rooms.debrief: Nothing here had to be solved — it was the engine's waste channel, where the Assay poured away everything their sort judged base. Every clustering has a flip side: deciding what belongs together is also deciding what gets left out.

rooms.title: The drowned sump

entry.title: The drowned sump
entry.text: The ladder lets you down into a dead-end pocket at the very bottom of the shaft, where the cast-off gathered and went foul years ago. A ruined vale-folk marker lies half-drowned in the wall — left to rot among the discards. There is nothing down here but the one way back up, and the water still rising.

rooms.technique: flavour — the drowned discard sump (no graded puzzle)
rooms.debrief: A dead-end, and meant to be one: the bottom of the waste stream, where everything the Assay cast off finally settled. Seeing it is the point — the sort's grand sacred pools have a foul twin, and the vale-folk's marker rotting here says who paid for the Assay's tidy kinds.

entry.text: Back up to the junction, and out across the shaft on a swaying bridge to a landing level with it on the far side. This font is not satisfied that you can sort — it wants you to weigh what you have sorted, to read a kind by its own measure. The makers' inscription gloats that most who came this far turned back here.

rooms.designNote: PUZZLE (verified). Dataset reliquary_phials. TYPE 3 CONSOLE-CHECK (summarise by cluster) — for puzzle-type variety; the student writes the pipeline, the check verifies. starterCode seeds: km <- kmeans(reliquary_phials[,c('clarity','mineral','resin','ash')], centers=3, nstart=25). TASK: compute the mean resin of each family and assign to `answer` the SIZE (number of phials) of the family with the highest average resin. Model soln: d <- cbind(reliquary_phials, cluster=km$cluster); tab <- aggregate(resin~cluster, d, mean); win <- tab$cluster[which.max(tab$resin)]; answer <- sum(km$cluster==win). check.requires: ['answer']; check.expr: answer == 6. ANSWER: 6 (highest-resin family mean 68.1 vs 28.3 vs 21.8; it is the size-6 family). HINT: cluster, then average resin within each family and look at how big the winning family is. Solving UNLOCKS diverter S3 -> D3. Lower shaft. NOTE the backtracker: throwing S3 opens the way to the boss and seals the way back; after the boss the player RETURNS here to throw S3 again (puzzle.json states 4->5). NEW ART.

rooms.title: The engine-hall

entry.title: The engine-hall
entry.text: One more bridge across the gulf, to the great hall at the far reach of the gallery — the Assay's masterwork, the whole engine grinding around you. Here they laid their final conceit for the greedy: it hands you every measure at once and dares you to trust the reading as it comes. A warning is cut into the wall, though it reads more like a taunt.

rooms.technique: flat clustering — k-means (the deciding assignment / choosing k)
rooms.debrief: The last decision was the hardest — the one assignment that only makes sense once you have seen how all the others fall. Setting it turned the whole machine over to its final, sorted state, and the floor below opened.

rooms.designNote: BOSS PUZZLE (verified; the SCALING TRAP). isBoss, puzzleType 2, deliverable figure + submitCodec. Dataset reliquary_phials, using ALL FIVE measures incl. weight. NAIVE (tempting, WRONG): kmeans(reliquary_phials[,c('clarity','mineral','resin','ash','weight')], centers=3, nstart=25) — weight (grains, thousands) drowns everything, ARI 0.07. CORRECT: kmeans(scale(reliquary_phials[,c('clarity','mineral','resin','ash','weight')]), centers=3, nstart=25). Q: 'Cluster the phials using ALL five measurements into 3 families. Which phial ends up in the same family as JASPER?' ANSWER: Selenite (scaled -> Jasper's true family A = Amber/Cinnabar/Onyx/Selenite/Verdigris; seed-robust in base R). DECOY (the trap): Antimony — Jasper's UNSCALED weight-band mate, what you get if you forget to scale. FILLER DISTRACTORS: Bloodstone, Galena, Chrysolite, Ochre (family B/C). DO NOT offer Onyx (in family A AND Jasper's weight band -> ambiguous). unlockedWhen allSolved [station1,station2,station3]. Solving UNLOCKS the final diverter (S4 -> D4). Throwing S4 gives 'no visible change' alone (puzzle.json) — the player must deduce that returning to S3 and re-throwing it opens the descent. NEW ART.

rooms.title: The drowned floor

entry.title: The drowned floor
entry.text: The final stair drops you into the risen flood on the cistern floor — knee-deep already and climbing — and there it is: the Assay's sorting made whole, three great pools towering from the water, the essences gathered into their kinds. Across the flood the vault stands sealed, the Wellheart behind it. Read the sort the way its makers did, before the water takes the floor.

rooms.technique: flat clustering — k-means (recognition: read the clusters)
rooms.debrief: The floor was the analysis made physical: the samples you had been routing all the way down, gathered at last into their pools — k clusters, each holding its own. Reading how many pools there are and how full each one is IS the output of k-means; counting them is literally what opened the door home.

authoring.scenePrompt: This is a panorama. A 360-degree view from the centre of the vast drowned floor of the Assay's engine — a great circular cistern chamber at the very bottom of the shaft, monumental in scale — the chamber wrapping continuously all the way around so the left and right edges meet seamlessly, its entire floor under a still sheet of risen flood-water that laps knee-high against every ledge, pillar and step, halfway up the stonework. Ahead, three enormous round stone basins rise from the flood, grand and deep and set well apart, each brimming with dark water and lit from beneath by a huge soft amber glow. From high in the darkness overhead, broad ribbons of waterfall pour straight down into the basins, gathered into distinct clusters rather than one sheet — the nearest basin fed by three falling ribbons, the next by two, the farthest by four — so the water pools into separate towering groups. To one side, a carved stone vault-keypad set into a colossal pillar, its glyphs lit amber just above the waterline, the reckoning that works the way out. Opposite, a huge closed stone vault door — the way home, and the Wellheart sealed behind it — its foot already drowned by the rising water. Around the rest of the chamber, colossal ribbed stonework streaked with mineral teal, half-submerged ledges, and the rope-and-plank descent climbing away up into shadow. Still black flood-water throwing mirror reflections of the towering amber basin-glow, cool teal shadow and warm amber light, drifting mist across the water, an unmistakable sense of the flood steadily rising, painterly, cinematic, richly detailed, monumental. No people, no lettering, no captions, no text.
